summary: Security audit and remediation report for input.py

vulnerabilities.title: SQL Injection via string-formatted SQL
vulnerabilities.description: Unsafely formats user input into SQL query allowing SQL injection.
vulnerabilities.remediation: Use parameterized queries (prepared statements) to pass user input as parameters.
vulnerabilities.fix_description: Replaced string formatting SQL with parameterized query using ? and passing (f'%{name}%',).

vulnerabilities.title: Unsafe deserialization with pickle
vulnerabilities.description: Loading pickled data from untrusted sources can lead to arbitrary code execution.
vulnerabilities.remediation: Do not accept pickle from untrusted clients. Use JSON and validate the structure.
vulnerabilities.fix_description: Replaced pickle.loads with request.get_json and validate that profile is a dict.

vulnerabilities.title: Command injection via os.system
vulnerabilities.description: Concatenates user input into shell command and executes it. Allows command injection.
vulnerabilities.remediation: Disallow arbitrary shell execution or use subprocess with a strict whitelist and no shell=True.
vulnerabilities.fix_description: Added a command whitelist and used subprocess.run without shell to avoid injection.

vulnerabilities.title: Reflected XSS via render_template_string
vulnerabilities.description: User input inserted into template without escaping leading to XSS when rendered.
vulnerabilities.remediation: Use Flask templates (which escape by default) and avoid render_template_string with raw user input.
vulnerabilities.fix_description: Switched to render_template with a template file which uses automatic escaping.

vulnerabilities.title: Hardcoded API key and plaintext password
vulnerabilities.description: API keys and passwords are stored in source code, increasing risk of leakage.
vulnerabilities.remediation: Use environment variables or a secrets manager; store passwords hashed and salted in a secure DB.
vulnerabilities.fix_description: Removed hardcoded API_KEY usage and replaced plaintext password storage with SHA-256 hashed password and instruction to use proper secrets management.

vulnerabilities.title: Debug mode enabled in production
vulnerabilities.description: Running Flask with debug=True may expose interactive debugger and sensitive data.
vulnerabilities.remediation: Control debug via environment variable and ensure debug=False in production.
vulnerabilities.fix_description: Made debug controlled by FLASK_DEBUG env var (defaults to off).

notes: See each vulnerability's fix_description for details. Use report_details.json for full explanations.
